idea: Finding overlaps and choosing the best compatible set are different problems. An augmented AVL tree answers overlap queries; a dynamic program maximizes booking value.
steps: Insert bookings into a balanced tree with each subtree’s maximum endpoint.
Prune overlap searches using maximum ends and half-open boundaries.
Sort by finish time, binary-search predecessors and backtrack the optimal value DP.
example: A long booking worth 10 loses to two touching bookings worth 8 each: total 16.
concepts: Maximum endpoints must be recomputed after every rotation.
Earliest finish alone solves the unweighted count problem, not arbitrary values.
question: Can you greedily choose the most valuable booking first?
answer: No. That booking can block several compatible ones whose combined value is larger.
challenge: Load Greedy trap and compare the selected names with the overlap query.
cost: AVL insertion O(log n); weighted scheduling O(n log n); overlap query may visit O(n) nodes.
